title: Prosper AI raises $30M from Andreessen Horowitz to scale the first AI platform to run the entire patient journey
summary: Prosper AI raised a $30M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz to scale the first AI platform that schedules patients, verifies benefits, and processes billing end-to-end.
body_text: New York, NY, June 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Prosper AI , the leading AI platform to run the entire patient journey, today announced a $30 million Series A financing led by Andreessen Horowitz (“a16z”), with participation from Base10 and continued support from Emergence Capital, Y Combinator, and Company Ventures The financing follows a period of rapid adoption and market acceleration. Since its last funding announcement six months ago, Prosper AI has grown revenue 5x, added more than 40 healthcare organizations as customers, expanded across more than 150,000 healthcare providers, and become the platform powering more than $1.3 billion in patient care. Today, Prosper AI wins 80% of competitive evaluations. Providers increasingly recognize that scheduling is only the first step in the patient journey. As healthcare organizations look to automate insurance verification, and patient billing alongside scheduling, Prosper AI is emerging as the platform of choice to power financially cleared appointments.Today, Prosper AI's customers span some of healthcare's most influential organizations, including PE-backed outpatient groups such as Preferred Dermatology, health systems such as Jackson Memorial Hospital—the second-largest hospital in Florida—and healthcare technology leaders such as Athenahealth, one of the largest ambulatory EHR platforms in the United States. Prosper AI: key numbers. Healthcare's Next AI Platform Won't Stop at Scheduling Every patient appointment depends on workflows that occur before and after care is delivered, from scheduling and insurance verification to patient billing and collections. Historically, these processes have been fragmented across disconnected teams and point solutions, creating +$450B in administrative waste while making healthcare more expensive and less transparent for patients. Where first-generation healthcare AI stopped at scheduling, Prosper AI manages the broader patient journey. The platform answers patient calls, schedules appointments directly in the EHR, verifies insurance benefits, automates patient billing, and contacts insurers on the phone when additional information is needed. By automating the patient journey end-to-end, Prosper AI helps providers lower administrative costs by +40% while giving patients visibility into their coverage and financial responsibility before care is delivered. The result is a single platform that manages both patient and payer workflows from appointment request through reimbursement. Winning the Most Competitive Evaluations in Healthcare AI As provider outpatient groups and health systems evaluate AI platforms, Prosper AI is increasingly emerging as the preferred solution. “We evaluated seven different vendors through an extensive RFP and live demonstration process and concluded that Prosper AI had the most comprehensive platform” said Jonathan Banta, CEO of The 44 Group, and Co-founder of The Executive Roundtable, a provider consortium representing more than 600 physicians. “The difference wasn't simply scheduling. Prosper AI was the only platform capable of handling insurance verification, patient financial responsibility, and the broader workflows required to support the entire patient journey.” “Out of the gate, Prosper AI was handling more than 50% of our patient conversations end-to-end, including complex cases involving real-time benefits verification,” said Noah England, COO of Piedmont Dermatology. “Many organizations using other AI solutions remain stuck at 20–30% automation because those systems stop at scheduling.” Patient Care Managed by Prosper AI. Enterprise Healthcare Platforms Are Choosing Prosper AI The shift toward comprehensive AI solutions beyond voice AI for scheduling is no longer limited to provider groups. Some of the largest healthcare technology companies have also selected Prosper AI following side-by-side evaluations against competing AI platforms. Athenahealth, one of the largest ambulatory EHR platforms in the United States covering +60M lives, selected Prosper AI after evaluating multiple AI solutions for internal voice AI workflows. Imagine Software, a leading healthcare software company serving more than 100,000 physicians and processing over $65 billion in claims annually, also selected Prosper AI after conducting a competitive evaluation. “We reviewed multiple AI platforms, and Prosper AI consistently delivered the strongest performance, now handling thousands of conversations per day across multiple clients on our platform,” said Sam Khashman, CEO of ImagineSoftware. “In repeated side-by-side evaluations, Prosper AI achieved the highest accuracy and completion rates.” Why Andreessen Horowitz and Base10 Invested "AI should make healthcare infinitely accessible," said Jay Rughani, Partner at Andreessen Horowitz. "Prosper AI stood out because of the scope of their ambition: they want to eliminate every administrative friction point between a patient and the care they need. What convinced us was the pattern we kept hearing from customers — providers would deploy Prosper AI for scheduling, then quickly ask them to take on insurance verification, then billing, and so on. That pull-through only happens when your technology can consistently guide patients through the care journey end-to-end. It's no surprise Prosper AI is winning the vast majority of competitive evaluations they enter." Adeyemi Ajao, Co-founder and Managing Partner at Base10 Partners “Prosper AI is leveraging agentic AI to transform the way provider groups and hospitals engage with patients, driving not only savings, but increased revenue and better patient experience". Building the AI Workforce for Healthcare Operations With the new funding, Prosper AI will expand its engineering and customer-facing teams, deepen integrations across the largest EHR platforms, and accelerate adoption across provider groups and health systems. “Healthcare providers don't want separate tools for scheduling, insurance verification, and billing,” said Xavier de Gracia, Co-Founder and Co-CEO of Prosper AI. “They want a single platform capable of managing the workflows that determine whether care happens and whether providers ultimately get paid. That's what we've built, and it's why providers, health systems, and healthcare technology companies are choosing Prosper AI.” Over time, Prosper AI aims to build the AI workforce that powers healthcare's administrative engine, eliminating waste, expanding access to care, and enabling providers to focus more of their time on patients. About Prosper AI Prosper AI is the agentic AI platform for patient access, and the first system to intelligently schedule patients, verify benefits, and process patient billing in one workflow. Built generative-first for both patient and payor calls, Prosper AI is live in 50+ outpatient groups and covers 150,000+ providers across more than 25 medical specialties, with deep integrations across athenahealth, ModMed, Veradigm, ECW, ImagineSoftware and other leading EHRs. The company was founded in 2023 by Xavier de Gracia and Josep Mingot and is headquartered in New York. Learn more at getprosper.ai About Andreessen Horowitz ‍ Andreessen Horowitz (aka a16z) is a venture capital firm that backs bold entrepreneurs building the future through technology. We are stage agnostic: We invest in seed to venture to growth-stage technology companies, across bio + healthcare, consumer and enterprise apps, crypto, fintech, infrastructure, and companies building toward American dynamism. a16z has over $90B under management across multiple funds. Base10 Partners Founded by Adeyemi Ajao and TJ Nahigian, Base10 is a San Francisco-based venture capital fund investing in founders who believe purpose is key to profits and companies that are automating sectors of the Real Economy, including transportation, retail, logistics, and construction. Through its program, The Advancement Initiative, Base10 aims to donate 50% of profits to underfunded colleges and universities to support financial aid and other key initiatives. Portfolio companies include Notion, Figma, Nubank, Stripe, Motive, Chili Piper, and Popmenu. Connect via www.base10.vc .

title: Hold on to the moments that matter
summary: Sudden cardiac arrest can devastate our most precious moments. Watch our latest video and see how AEDs and fast action can help keep the picture whole and the future bright.
body_text: 1-minute read Be ready to act when sudden cardiac arrest interrupts the everyday Life is built from small moments—coffee before sunrise, sideline cheers, a hand squeezed at the right time. Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) can happen to anyone, anywhere, interrupting those moments without warning. Our latest video shows us what’s worth protecting and how being prepared can help. We hope it sparks conversations about readiness in your home, school, workplace and community, and encourages simple steps to be better prepared for cardiac emergencies. At Stryker, we understand that being prepared is a community effort. Awareness, education and access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs) can help more people respond in the first moments, when every second matters. This video reminds us that anyone can play a role—from bystanders who call for help, to first responders and clinical teams who continue care. It’s not just about SCA. It’s about savoring everyday moments and once-in-a-lifetime milestones with the people we love, and doing what we can to help more of them happen. It’s about keeping the picture whole and celebrating those who are still here, building new memories after the unthinkable. We support that readiness through innovation, training and advocacy. Our aim is to help more people stay here—still here—with the ones who love them. Related Workplace and public safety An AED program is a critical link in the chain of survival of a sudden cardiac arrest, empowering you to deliver lifesaving intervention before first responders arrive. With more than a million AEDs deployed globally, Stryker offers diverse options and deep expertise to help you choose the right device and cost-effectively manage your community AED program. Learn more Sudden cardiac arrest vs heart attack: what you need to know Heart attacks and sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) are two very different events, but people often confuse the two. Understanding the difference could help save a life. Learn more Survivor: Mark Dundore Mark, who has had atrial fibrillation (Afib) since 2009, began to feel unwell and had difficulty breathing after lunch. Once Mark became unresponsive, coworkers began chest compressions and used an AED they installed just three weeks prior. The presence of this device on-site helped saved Mark's life. Learn more LIFEPAK CR2 defibrillator The LIFEPAK CR2 AED response system empowers bystanders to help save lives. Innovative, easy-to-operate technology allows continuous CPR and helps streamline communication across the system of care. Learn more

title: Unified Logs is now in open beta
summary: One searchable view for logs across every Supabase service, with live tail, filtering, and a timeline.
body_text: Today Unified Logs enters open beta. It brings logs from every service in your project into one searchable view: the API gateway, Postgres, Auth, Storage, PostgREST, Realtime, and the connection poolers. Before this, debugging a single request meant jumping between separate log pages. You checked the API gateway logs, then Postgres logs, then Auth logs, each with its own filters and its own tab. Correlating a request across services was slow, and by the time you found the right page the context was gone. Unified Logs puts all of that in one place. One stream across your services # Open Logs in the dashboard and you see every event as it happens, newest first. Each row shows the timestamp, the service, the method, the path, and the status. One row might be an API request, the next a Postgres connection, the next an Auth event, all in the same table. The sidebar lets you narrow the stream by log type. Turn off Storage and Realtime to focus on Postgres. Turn everything back on to see the full picture. The counts next to each type update as you filter, so you know how much traffic each service is producing. Filter and search # The filter bar at the top understands the shape of your logs. Filter by log type, level, status, method, or pathname, and combine those filters however you need. You can also run a free-text search across the event message to find a specific request. Filters live in the URL, so you can share a link to exactly what you are looking at with a teammate. Live tail # Click Live to stream new events into the table as they arrive. This is the fastest way to watch a deploy, reproduce a bug, or confirm that traffic is reaching the right service. Stop the stream at any point to inspect what you have without new rows pushing it down. A timeline you can read # The histogram above the table shows log volume over your selected time range, colored by level so errors and warnings stand out from successful requests. A spike in red tells you where to look. Select a range on the timeline to zoom into that window. Follow a request through every service # Click a row to open the detail panel. Instead of a wall of JSON, you see the request as it moved through your project: the network timing, the gateway, the database query, the Auth check. Each service adds its own block with the fields that matter. The raw JSON is still there in a second tab when you need it. Send logs anywhere # Unified Logs is for debugging inside the dashboard. When you want to keep logs long term or pull them into your own observability tooling, set up a Log Drain and forward events to the destination of your choice. Try it # Unified Logs is rolling out to all projects during open beta. Open the Logs section of your project to start using it. If you want the previous experience back, the "Go back to old logs" button switches you to the classic Logs Explorer at any time. This is a beta, and we want your feedback. Tell us what is missing, what is slow, and what you want to filter on next.

title: AI Revenue Platform for Law Firms: What It Is - PointOne
summary: Why the future of legal AI isn't another point solution—it's a single foundation for every revenue workflow.
body_text: AI Summary AI revenue platforms connect timekeeping, billing, pricing, and analytics through one record of attorney work. They use activity across email, documents, meetings, and other systems to capture time and manage revenue. The same data can flag billing issues, forecast budgets, analyze write-offs, and guide pricing. Firms should prioritize legal-work context, flexible time entry, and integration with existing financial systems. PointOne’s AI revenue platform combines time capture, billing compliance, pricing intelligence, analytics, and AI assistants without requiring firms to replace their current practice management or financial software. For decades, legal technology has treated revenue as a series of disconnected workflows. Timekeeping. Billing. Pricing. Pre-bill review. Reporting. Each has traditionally been handled by a different system, with professionals manually moving information from one step to the next. Artificial intelligence is changing that model. Instead of optimizing each workflow independently, a new generation of software is creating a single understanding of the work performed by attorneys and using that information to improve every stage of the revenue lifecycle. This is the idea behind the AI Revenue Platform . What Is an AI Revenue Platform? An AI revenue platform creates a structured, continuously updated record of the work performed across a law firm. Rather than asking attorneys to reconstruct their day from memory, the platform observes work as it happens across email, documents, meetings, calendars, research, phone calls, and other business systems. That record becomes the foundation for multiple revenue workflows, including: AI-assisted time capture Billing compliance Pre-bill review Pricing and matter budgeting Revenue analytics AI assistants Future AI workflows Instead of building separate systems for each of these functions, an AI revenue platform uses the same underlying data across them all. Why Timekeeping Alone Is No Longer Enough AI timekeeping has become one of the fastest-growing categories in legal technology because it solves an obvious problem: attorneys dislike entering time, and firms lose revenue when work goes unrecorded. Recovering that lost time is valuable. But once AI understands the work performed, stopping at time entry leaves significant value untapped. The same information that generates a time entry can also answer questions such as: Does this narrative comply with the client's billing guidelines? Is the matter likely to exceed its budget? Are attorneys consistently under-recording certain types of work? Which clients generate the highest write-offs? How profitable is this practice area? How should future matters be priced? The opportunity is no longer simply to automate timesheets. It is to improve how firms manage revenue from the moment work begins until an invoice is paid. The Shift from Point Solutions to Platforms Law firms have historically assembled revenue operations using multiple products. One system captures time. Another reviews bills. Another manages pricing. Another provides analytics. Each application stores overlapping information, creating duplicate data, inconsistent reporting, and disconnected workflows. An AI revenue platform takes a different approach. Instead of optimizing individual steps, it creates a shared foundation that supports every revenue workflow. As new AI capabilities emerge, they can be built on the same record of work rather than requiring another standalone application. What Should Firms Look for? Not every AI platform is designed with the same philosophy. When evaluating vendors, firms should look beyond time capture and ask broader questions. 1. Does it understand work, or simply record activity? Capturing clicks and application usage is only the beginning. The platform should understand client context, matters, billing narratives, and professional work well enough to produce meaningful outputs. 2. Can attorneys work the way they already do? Adoption depends on flexibility. Some professionals prefer passive capture, others manual entry, voice dictation, timers, or reconstructing their day after the fact. The platform should support different working styles rather than forcing a single workflow. 3. Does the same data power multiple workflows? Time capture should not exist in isolation. The same underlying record should support billing compliance, pre-bill review, pricing, analytics, and future AI capabilities. 4. Does it integrate with existing financial systems? Most firms are not replacing their practice management or financial software. The best AI platforms extend existing systems rather than requiring a complete migration. 5. Is the platform designed for the future? AI capabilities are evolving rapidly. Firms should consider whether they are investing in a collection of point solutions or a platform that can support new workflows as they emerge. Why We Believe the Market Is Moving Toward AI Revenue Platforms The legal industry is entering a new phase of AI adoption. The first wave focused on automating individual tasks such as drafting documents, researching cases, or recording time. The next wave will focus on connecting those workflows together. Revenue is one of the clearest examples. Every billing decision begins with understanding the work that was performed. Once that understanding exists, AI can assist with compliance, pricing, forecasting, analytics, and operational decision-making. Rather than solving one workflow at a time, firms will increasingly adopt platforms that use a single understanding of work to improve the entire revenue lifecycle. PointOne's Approach PointOne was built around this philosophy. Rather than treating AI time capture as the end goal, PointOne creates a structured, AI-generated record of work that becomes the foundation for revenue operations. That same record powers AI-assisted time capture, billing compliance, pre-bill review, pricing intelligence, operational analytics, and AI assistants, while integrating with existing practice management and financial systems. We believe the future of legal technology is not a collection of disconnected AI tools. It is a shared foundation that allows every revenue workflow to become more intelligent over time. The AI revenue platform is the beginning of that shift. Your AI-powered firm starts here Book a demo Your AI-powered firm starts here Book a demo Your AI-powered firm starts here Book a demo How does AI improve law firm timekeeping and billing? AI can identify work performed across email, documents, meetings, calendars, research, and phone calls, then generate suggested time entries and billing narratives. It can also check entries against client billing guidelines and surface possible errors before invoices are submitted. What is the difference between AI timekeeping software and an AI revenue platform? AI timekeeping software primarily focuses on capturing billable work and generating time entries. An AI revenue platform uses that same work data across the wider revenue cycle, including billing compliance, pre-bill review, matter budgeting, pricing, forecasting, and profitability analysis. Can an AI revenue platform integrate with existing law firm software? Yes. AI revenue platforms can integrate with practice management, time and billing, document management, calendar, email, and financial systems. Firms can extend their existing technology stack without necessarily replacing their core financial or practice management platform. What should law firms consider when choosing an AI revenue platform? Firms should assess how accurately the platform understands legal work, whether it accommodates different attorney timekeeping habits, which revenue workflows use the collected data, and how it integrates with existing systems. Security, billing-guideline controls, implementation requirements, reporting capabilities, and vendor experience with law firm workflows should also be reviewed.

title: A importância dos dados na construção de estratégias de engajamento com o consumidor digital em 2025
summary: Brasília marcou o início do "Conexão Comscore – Onde os Dados se Encontram", um evento especialmente pensado para conectar o mercado e profissionais em torno de dados e estratégias digitais pelo Brasil. Neste blog, destacamos os principais insights e tendências discutidos durante o encontro.
body_text: Em 2025, mais do que nunca, engajar consumidores exige mais do que presença digital — exige inteligência sobre seus hábitos, plataformas preferidas, necessidades e expectativas. A partir de dados confiáveis e bem analisados, é possível transformar métricas em ações que geram relevância, vínculo e resultados. Foi com esse olhar que realizamos o Conexão Comscore em Brasília, em 16 de julho. O encontro reuniu mais de 60 convidados, entre representantes comerciais, agências, anunciantes, veículos e governo, para discutir os caminhos da mensuração digital e apresentar dados inéditos sobre o comportamento da população nas plataformas digitais. Comportamento digital e o poder da segmentação O comportamento digital dos brasileiros revela um cenário de alta conectividade, hábitos consolidados e decisões cada vez mais mediadas pelas plataformas digitais. Em fevereiro a Comscore registrou, 116 milhões de usuários digitais ativos¹ no Brasil, com uma distribuição que evidencia a diversidade do ecossistema: 50 milhões pertencem às classes A/B, 51 milhões à classe C e 15 milhões às classes D/E ². Essa amplitude reflete não apenas o alcance da internet, mas a profundidade com que ela permeia a rotina das pessoas. Hoje, 97% dos brasileiros acompanham os acontecimentos atuais pela internet³, e 73% a utilizam como principal forma de entretenimento. A jornada digital também se intensifica nas decisões de consumo: 68% preferem fazer compras pelo celular, enquanto 67% usam a web para planejar suas viagens⁴. No campo financeiro, 66% afirmam recorrer ao cartão de crédito mesmo sem saldo disponível, e, no lazer, 65% escolhem viajar dentro do país — um dado que ilustra a influência do digital tanto nas aspirações quanto nas escolhas práticas do cotidiano. Essas evidências constroem o retrato de um consumidor que transita entre canais, formatos e plataformas com fluidez. Para as marcas, isso representa a necessidade de estratégias de engajamento baseadas em dados, personalização e contexto. Entender como se conecta é apenas o começo; o diferencial está em saber quando e com que conteúdo criar relevância real na vida digital das pessoas. Centro-Oeste em dados: comportamento, consumo e conexão O Centro-Oeste brasileiro se destaca pela maturidade digital, reunindo 21 milhões de compradores conectados⁵ — dos quais 85% acessam regularmente sites de varejo. Em fevereiro de 2025, a Shopee liderou os acessos na região com 1,78 milhão de visitantes únicos⁵, seguida por nomes consolidados como Mercado Livre, Amazon, Magazine Luiza e Alibaba. O volume de 1 milhão de acessos ao portal dos Correios no Centro-Oeste, em abril de 2025⁶, destaca o papel estratégico da entrega e da infraestrutura no ecossistema digital regional Além do consumo, o comportamento digital na região também revela um público consciente e informado: 9,8 milhões de pessoas afirmam possuir plano de saúde⁴, enquanto 2,9 milhões declaram utilizar preservativos ao iniciar um novo relacionamento⁵ — um indicativo relevante de decisões orientadas por autocuidado e acesso à informação. A região Centro-Oeste assume papel estratégico para empresas, agências e entidades governamentais. Sua relevância cresce à medida que o público local se mostra cada vez mais digitalizado e engajado. Para organizações que desejam se posicionar de forma assertiva nesse cenário, os dados apontam caminhos claros: é essencial adaptar linguagem, canais e propostas de valor a uma audiência conectada, participativa e habituada a tomar decisões relevantes no ambiente digital. A força dos aplicativos e o domínio do tempo Em um cenário cada vez mais multiplataforma e orientado por múltiplos formatos de conteúdo, os apps seguem no centro da jornada digital. Em 2025⁷, 121,8 milhões de brasileiros acessaram aplicativos, com uma média de 101,5 horas mensais por visitante — 18 vezes mais tempo do que o dedicado ao mobile web. Entre as categorias mais acessadas estão portais (128,9 milhões), entretenimento (128 milhões), serviços (123,4 milhões), busca (118,8 milhões) e notícias (117,1 milhões). Esses dados reforçam a importância de estratégias mobile-first. Marcas que investirem em experiências otimizadas para apps com navegação fluida, personalização e boa usabilidade, estarão mais bem posicionadas para reter e engajar suas audiências. Notícias em Rede: Quando a Informação Ganha Voz nas Redes Sociais O Brasil se destaca no consumo de notícias e informação pelas redes sociais, são 6,4 bilhões de interações com publicações jornalísticas nas redes em 2024 liderando a América Latina⁸. O portal Metrópoles, foi o mais acessado (73,5 milhões)⁹, seguido por Globo Notícias, UOL, R7 e Diários Associados. Essa evidência reforça o papel dos conteúdos informativos no engajamento digital — sobretudo quando conectados a plataformas sociai Com 86% da população brasileira conectada às redes sociais em abril de 2025 e uma média de 48 horas mensais por visitante único, está claro que as plataformas digitais não são apenas canais de entretenimento, são espaços centrais de atenção, influência e decisão. O YouTube lidera em alcance, com 113,6 milhões de usuários¹⁰, mostrando sua força como plataforma de massa. Já o Instagram, com 17,8 horas por usuário¹¹ mês, segue como o território da curadoria pessoal e das narrativas visuais. Um destaque para as plataformas de vídeos nativos, como Kwai que teve um destaque de 17,6 horas por visitante¹² reforça que há espaço para formatos ágeis e públicos emergentes. E o TikTok, com aumento de 27% na produção de vídeos entre janeiro e maio de 2025¹³, consolida sua posição como motor de tendências e comportamento. Mais do que buscar visibilidade, as marcas precisam compreender o que realmente impulsiona o engajamento: tempo de permanência, recorrência, formato nativo e, sobretudo, autenticidade. Em um cenário multitela, com usuários cada vez mais seletivos, quem não souber entregar valor real em cada segundo corre o risco de simplesmente ser ignorado. O setor financeiro na era do digital banking A alta conectividade do brasileiro, com 86% da população ativa nas redes sociais e milhões de usuários que priorizam o acesso mobile, tem acelerado a transformação do setor financeiro. Em maio de 2025, os serviços financeiros digitais registraram 109,8 milhões de usuários¹⁴ com um total de 14 bilhões de minutos consumidos. Isso representa uma média de 1 hora e 34 minutos por pessoa no mês. O segmento bancário concentra a maior parte dessa audiência, com 86,2 milhões de usuários¹⁵, seguido por serviços de pagamento (53,6 milhões), investimentos (5,5 milhões) e seguros (4,1 milhões). A jornada digital já é realidade, especialmente nos bancos nativos digitais. O Nubank lidera entre contas correntes, com 20,2 milhões de visitantes únicos, enquanto a Caixa Econômica Federal se destaca nas contas de poupança, com 23,7 milhões de acessos ¹⁶ Os dados revelam um consumidor cada vez mais conectado, exigente e habituado à agilidade do ambiente digital. Para se manterem relevantes, as instituições financeiras precisam ir além da digitalização, oferecendo experiências simples, confiáveis e personalizadas que acompanhem o novo comportamento do brasileiro online. Conclusão: dados que orientam e conectam Após analisar o cenário digital brasileiro em 2025, destacamos quatro chaves para conectar com o consumidor de forma relevante e eficaz: 1. O Brasil digital é múltiplo e dinâmico Para começar, é fundamental adotar uma estratégia realmente integrada e multiplataformas . Com consumidores cada vez mais conectados e ativos em diferentes ambientes digitais, as marcas precisam estar onde seu público está — com conteúdo adaptado aos hábitos e preferências de cada canal. 2. Dados oferecem caminhos, mas o diferencial está na execução A extração e interpretação de dados são apenas o ponto de partida. O verdadeiro valor está em saber interpretá-los e aplicá-los de forma estratégica, personalizada e adequada ao contexto. 3. Conhecer o consumidor exige uma visão além dos números Para gerar conexões autênticas, é essencial considerar não apenas métricas, mas também aspectos sociais, regionais e emocionais do comportamento digital. 4.
